problem: The length of a curve $y=f(x)$ is given by ${\int }_{0}^{1/2}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{(1-x)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.$ Which of the following could be  an equation for this curve?
worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We're given that 

$$
L={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{(1-x)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Comparing the above with the arc length formula, we see that we must have

$$
[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}=\frac{1}{(1-x)^{2}}\,⟹\,{f}^{′}(x)=\pm \frac{1}{1-x}.
$$

Integrating the above equation with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\pm \int \frac{1}{1-x}\text{ d}x \\  & =\pm (-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-x|)+C \\  & =\pm \operatorname{ln}⁡(1-x)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given options, the only one that has the required form is $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-x)+7.$
